title: One position. Borrow or sell.
text: A locked position can still be valuable when you need liquidity today. Lockpad gives its owner two choices: borrow against it, or sell the payout right.

title: Built with four NEAR contracts
text: This prototype uses four NEAR contracts: a reference vault, a funded lending pool, a marketplace, and a test token. Alice owns a one thousand token position.

title: Borrow 650 TUSD. Repay 663.
text: The pool can offer six hundred and fifty tokens now. With a one-time two percent fee, Alice would repay six hundred and sixty-three before the original maturity. These are illustrative prototype terms.

title: 650 TUSD reaches Alice’s wallet
text: Alice accepts. Her payout right secures the loan, and six hundred and fifty test tokens reach her wallet. The principal stays in its source vault.

title: Repay 663 TUSD. Recover the same NFT.
text: She repays six hundred and sixty-three tokens. The same payout NFT returns to her wallet, with its principal and original maturity preserved.

title: List instead. Choose 920 TUSD.
text: If the borrowing offer is too low, Alice can list instead. Here, she chooses nine hundred and twenty tokens. A buyer must accept that price.

title: The buyer gets the original NFT
text: Bob checks the position, reviews the price, and buys it. The original payout NFT reaches his wallet before the marketplace credits Alice's sale proceeds.

title: Alice withdraws 920 TUSD
text: Alice withdraws her nine hundred and twenty tokens. The sale gives her liquidity while the underlying principal remains locked.

title: Local time advances. Same maturity.
text: We advance local Sandbox time without changing the original maturity.

title: Bob claims the full 1,000 TUSD
text: Bob then claims the full one thousand token payout from the reference vault. The app marks his position redeemed.

title: A working prototype before mainnet
text: Each action leaves a receipt. This is proposed work before mainnet, using zero-value tokens. External DEX positions need a supported way to transfer or secure their payout rights.
